name: Tale
hook: Shared project tasks and files for people and AI agents.
bullets: Task briefs and attachments in a shared project workspace
Explicitly start configured agent work and review reports and files
MIT Community software; infrastructure and model costs are separate
setupSteps: Follow the official self-hosting quickstart at docs.tale.dev
Configure providers and an agent harness for your deployment
Create a project and a task with its brief and attachments
Assign an agent, explicitly start work, then review the report and files
details: Tale is a self-hosted project workspace where people and configured AI agents share tasks, files, knowledge, and reviewed outputs. It offers an alternative for the shared task-and-file workflow found in tools such as Asana; this does not imply complete feature parity or a migration integration. Assignment alone does not start agent work: the user explicitly starts it and reviews the resulting report and files. The Community edition is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, with infrastructure and model-provider costs paid separately. Installation and provider configuration require operating your own deployment.
